editorial:
Imagine being a regular student who tries weed for the first time and suddenly sees a gold mine. That is exactly how things kick off here. You get to follow a guy who is not just looking to chill, but wants to turn his new hobby into a massive business empire. The vibe is very laid-back but chaotic, capturing that wild 70s energy where everything feels a bit loose and unpredictable. It feels like a ride with a friend who has a great idea that is probably going to end in a total disaster, and you are just along for the ride.

What really works is how the stakes keep climbing. Just when you think he has it figured out, the police and the mob show up to crash the party. The pacing is snappy, and the comedy comes from seeing a naive student try to act like a big-shot boss. While some of the jokes feel a bit dated, the energy keeps you interested. If you want to see this one, you should definitely grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get those vintage colors popping, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: In the final act, the main character realizes that playing with the mafia is a losing game. After a series of wild chases and narrow escapes, he manages to outsmart both the cops and the gangsters. He ends up losing his business empire, but he saves his own skin in the process. The movie wraps up with him returning to a simpler life, having learned that fast money usually comes with too many dangerous strings attached.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves vintage comedies and underdog stories.
